verses.original: Ἀγρίππας δὲ πρὸς τὸν Παῦλον ἔφη Ἐπιτρέπεταί σοι ὑπὲρ σεαυτοῦ λέγειν Τότε ὁ Παῦλος ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἀπελογεῖτο
verses.transliteration: Agrippas de pros ton Paulon ephē Epitrepetai soi hyper seautou legein Tote ho Paulos ekteinas tēn cheira apelogeito
verses.literal: Agrippa said to Paul You have permission to speak for yourself Then Paul stretched out his hand and began his defense
verses.literalPt: Agripa disse a Paulo: A ti se te permite fazer a tua defesa. Então, Paulo, estendendo a mão, começou a defender-se:

verses.original: Περὶ πάντων ὧν ἐγκαλοῦμαι ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα ἥγημαι ἐμαυτὸν μακάριον ἐπὶ σοῦ μέλλων σήμερον ἀπολογεῖσθαι
verses.transliteration: Peri pantōn hōn enkaloumai hypo Ioudaiōn basileu Agrippa hēgēmai emauton makarion epi sou mellōn sēmeron apologeisthai
verses.literal: King Agrippa I consider myself fortunate to stand before you today to defend myself against all the accusations of the Jews
verses.literalPt: Julgo-me feliz, ó rei Agripa, por ter de fazer hoje, perante ti, a minha defesa de tudo o que me acusam os judeus,

verses.original: μάλιστα γνώστην ὄντα σε πάντων τῶν κατὰ Ἰουδαίους ἐθῶν τε καὶ ζητημάτων διὸ δέομαι μακροθύμως ἀκοῦσαί μου
verses.transliteration: malista gnōstēn onta se pantōn tōn kata Ioudaious ethōn te kai zētēmatōn dio deomai makrothymōs akousai mou
verses.literal: especially since you are acquainted with all the Jewish customs and controversies I beg you therefore to listen to me patiently
verses.literalPt: mormente porque és versado em todos os costumes e questões que há entre eles; pelo que te rogo que me ouças com paciência.

verses.original: Τὴν μὲν οὖν βίωσίν μου τὴν ἐκ νεότητος τὴν ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς γενομένην ἐν τῷ ἔθνει μου ἔν τε Ἱεροσολύμοις ἴσασι πάντες οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι
verses.transliteration: Tēn men oun biōsin mou tēn ek neotētos tēn ap’ archēs genomenēn en tō ethnei mou en te Hierosolymois isasi pantes hoi Ioudaioi
verses.literal: Surely . . . all the Jews know how I have lived - from my earliest - childhood among my own . . . people and also in Jerusalem
verses.literalPt: Quanto à minha vida durante a mocidade, que passei desde o princípio entre o meu povo e em Jerusalém, sabem-na todos os judeus,

verses.original: προγινώσκοντές με ἄνωθεν ἐὰν θέλωσι μαρτυρεῖν ὅτι κατὰ τὴν ἀκριβεστάτην αἵρεσιν τῆς ἡμετέρας θρησκείας ἔζησα Φαρισαῖος
verses.transliteration: proginōskontes me anōthen ean thelōsi martyrein hoti kata tēn akribestatēn hairesin tēs hēmeteras thrēskeias ezēsa Pharisaios
verses.literal: They have known me for a long time and can testify if they are willing that I lived as a Pharisee adhering to the strictest sect of our religion
verses.literalPt: conhecendo-me desde o princípio (se quiserem dar disso testemunho), como vivi fariseu conforme a seita mais severa da nossa religião.

verses.original: Καὶ νῦν ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι τῆς εἰς τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν ἐπαγγελίας γενομένης ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἕστηκα κρινόμενος
verses.transliteration: Kai nyn ep’ elpidi tēs eis tous pateras hēmōn epangelias genomenēs hypo tou Theou hestēka krinomenos
verses.literal: And now I stand on trial because of my hope in the promise that - God made to our fathers
verses.literalPt: Agora, estou aqui para ser julgado pela esperança da promessa feita por Deus a nossos pais,

verses.original: εἰς ἣν τὸ δωδεκάφυλον ἡμῶν ἐν ἐκτενείᾳ νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν λατρεῦον ἐλπίζει καταντῆσαι περὶ ἧς ἐλπίδος ἐγκαλοῦμαι ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων βασιλεῦ
verses.transliteration: eis hēn to dōdekaphylon hēmōn en ekteneia nykta kai hēmeran latreuon elpizei katantēsai peri hēs elpidos enkaloumai hypo Ioudaiōn basileu
verses.literal: the promise our twelve tribes are hoping to see fulfilled as they earnestly serve God . . . . . . day and night It is because of this hope O king that I am accused by the Jews
verses.literalPt: a qual as nossas doze tribos, servindo a Deus fervorosamente de noite e de dia, esperam alcançar; por causa dessa esperança, ó rei, sou acusado pelos judeus.

verses.original: τί ἄπιστον κρίνεται παρ’ ὑμῖν εἰ ὁ Θεὸς νεκροὺς ἐγείρει
verses.transliteration: ti apiston krinetai par’ hymin ei ho Theos nekrous egeirei
verses.literal: Why would any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead
verses.literalPt: Por que é que se julga entre vós coisa incrível ressuscitar Deus aos mortos?

verses.original: Ἐγὼ μὲν οὖν ἔδοξα ἐμαυτῷ πρὸς τὸ ὄνομα Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου δεῖν πολλὰ ἐναντία πρᾶξαι
verses.transliteration: Egō men oun edoxa emautō pros to onoma Iēsou tou Nazōraiou dein polla enantia praxai
verses.literal: So then . . . I too was convinced that I ought to do all I could to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth
verses.literalPt: Eu, na verdade, entendia que devia fazer toda a oposição ao nome de Jesus, o Nazareno;

verses.original: ὃ καὶ ἐποίησα ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις καὶ πολλούς τε τῶν ἁγίων ἐγὼ ἐν φυλακαῖς κατέκλεισα τὴν παρὰ τῶν ἀρχιερέων ἐξουσίαν λαβών ἀναιρουμένων τε αὐτῶν κατήνεγκα ψῆφον
verses.transliteration: ho kai epoiēsa en Hierosolymois kai pollous te tōn hagiōn egō en phylakais katekleisa tēn para tōn archiereōn exousian labōn anairoumenōn te autōn katēnenka psēphon
verses.literal: And that is what I did in Jerusalem With authority from the chief priests - I put many of the saints in prison and when they were condemned to death I cast my vote against them . . .
verses.literalPt: e assim o fiz em Jerusalém. Tendo recebido autoridade dos principais sacerdotes, eu não somente encarcerei muitos santos, como também dei o meu voto contra estes quando os matavam;

verses.original: καὶ κατὰ πάσας τὰς συναγωγὰς πολλάκις τιμωρῶν αὐτοὺς ἠνάγκαζον βλασφημεῖν περισσῶς τε ἐμμαινόμενος αὐτοῖς ἐδίωκον ἕως καὶ εἰς τὰς ἔξω πόλεις
verses.transliteration: kai kata pasas tas synagōgas pollakis timōrōn autous ēnankazon blasphēmein perissōs te emmainomenos autois ediōkon heōs kai eis tas exō poleis
verses.literal: I frequently had them punished in the synagogues and I tried to make them blaspheme In my raging fury . . . against them I even went to foreign cities to persecute them
verses.literalPt: e, muitas vezes, castigando-os por todas as sinagogas, obrigava-os a blasfemar e, enfurecido cada vez mais contra eles, perseguia-os até nas cidades estrangeiras.

verses.original: Ἐν οἷς πορευόμενος εἰς τὴν Δαμασκὸν μετ’ ἐξουσίας καὶ ἐπιτροπῆς τῆς τῶν ἀρχιερέων
verses.transliteration: En hois poreuomenos eis tēn Damaskon met’ exousias kai epitropēs tēs tōn archiereōn
verses.literal: In this pursuit I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests
verses.literalPt: Nesse intuito, indo a Damasco com autoridade e comissão dos principais sarcedotes,

verses.original: ἡμέρας μέσης κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν εἶδον βασιλεῦ οὐρανόθεν ὑπὲρ τὴν λαμπρότητα τοῦ ἡλίου περιλάμψαν με φῶς καὶ τοὺς σὺν ἐμοὶ πορευομένους
verses.transliteration: hēmeras mesēs kata tēn hodon eidon basileu ouranothen hyper tēn lamprotēta tou hēliou perilampsan me phōs kai tous syn emoi poreuomenous
verses.literal: About noon . . . O king as I was on the road I saw a light from heaven . . . brighter than the sun shining around me and my companions . . . . . . . . .
verses.literalPt: ao meio-dia, ó rei, vi no caminho uma luz do céu, mais brilhante que o sol, a qual resplandeceu em torno de mim e dos que iam comigo.

verses.original: πάντων τε καταπεσόντων ἡμῶν εἰς τὴν γῆν ἤκουσα φωνὴν λέγουσαν πρός με τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ Σαοὺλ Σαούλ τί με διώκεις σκληρόν σοι πρὸς κέντρα λακτίζειν
verses.transliteration: pantōn te katapesontōn hēmōn eis tēn gēn ēkousa phōnēn legousan pros me tē Hebraidi dialektō Saoul Saoul ti me diōkeis sklēron soi pros kentra laktizein
verses.literal: We all fell to the ground and I heard a voice say to me in Hebrew . . . Saul Saul why do you persecute Me It is hard for you to kick against the goads
verses.literalPt: Caindo nós por terra, ouvi uma voz que me dizia em língua hebraica: Saulo, Saulo, por que me persegues? Dura coisa te é recalcitrar contra os aguilhões.

verses.original: Ἐγὼ δὲ εἶπα Τίς εἶ Κύριε Ὁ δὲ Κύριος εἶπεν Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὃν σὺ διώκεις
verses.transliteration: Egō de eipa Tis ei Kyrie Ho de Kyrios eipen Egō eimi Iēsous hon sy diōkeis
verses.literal: Who are You Lord I asked I am Jesus whom you are persecuting the Lord replied
verses.literalPt: Eu perguntei: Quem és, Senhor? Respondeu-me o Senhor: Eu sou Jesus, a quem tu persegues.

verses.original: ἀλλὰ ἀνάστηθι καὶ στῆθι ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας σου εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ὤφθην σοι προχειρίσασθαί σε ὑπηρέτην καὶ μάρτυρα ὧν τε εἶδές με ὧν τε ὀφθήσομαί σοι
verses.transliteration: alla anastēthi kai stēthi epi tous podas sou eis touto gar ōphthēn soi procheirisasthai se hypēretēn kai martyra hōn te eides me hōn te ophthēsomai soi
verses.literal: But get up and stand on your feet For I have appeared to you to appoint you as a servant and as a witness of what you have seen from Me and what I will show you
verses.literalPt: Mas levanta-te e fica em pé; pois para isso te apareci a fim de te constituir ministro e testemunha das coisas em que me viste e daquelas em que me hei de manifestar,

verses.original: ἐξαιρούμενός σε ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἐθνῶν εἰς οὓς ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω σε
verses.transliteration: exairoumenos se ek tou laou kai ek tōn ethnōn eis hous egō apostellō se
verses.literal: I will rescue you from your own people and from the Gentiles I am sending you to them
verses.literalPt: livrando-te do povo e dos gentios, aos quais eu te envio,

verses.original: ἀνοῖξαι ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν τοῦ ἐπιστρέψαι ἀπὸ σκότους εἰς φῶς καὶ τῆς ἐξουσίας τοῦ Σατανᾶ ἐπὶ τὸν Θεόν τοῦ λαβεῖν αὐτοὺς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν καὶ κλῆρον ἐν τοῖς ἡγιασμένοις πίστει τῇ εἰς ἐμέ
verses.transliteration: anoixai ophthalmous autōn tou epistrepsai apo skotous eis phōs kai tēs exousias tou Satana epi ton Theon tou labein autous aphesin hamartiōn kai klēron en tois hēgiasmenois pistei tē eis eme
verses.literal: to open their eyes so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those sanctified by faith in Me
verses.literalPt: para lhes abrir os olhos, a fim de que se convertam das trevas à luz e, do poder de Satanás, a Deus, para que, pela fé em mim, recebam remissão de pecados e herança entre os santificados.

verses.original: Ὅθεν βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα οὐκ ἐγενόμην ἀπειθὴς τῇ οὐρανίῳ ὀπτασίᾳ
verses.transliteration: Hothen basileu Agrippa ouk egenomēn apeithēs tē ouraniō optasia
verses.literal: So then King Agrippa I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision
verses.literalPt: Por isso, ó rei Agripa, não fui desobediente à visão celestial,

verses.original: ἀλλὰ τοῖς ἐν Δαμασκῷ πρῶτόν τε καὶ Ἱεροσολύμοις πᾶσάν τε τὴν χώραν τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἀπήγγελλον μετανοεῖν καὶ ἐπιστρέφειν ἐπὶ τὸν Θεόν ἄξια τῆς μετανοίας ἔργα πράσσοντας
verses.transliteration: alla tois en Damaskō prōton te kai Hierosolymois pasan te tēn chōran tēs Ioudaias kai tois ethnesin apēngellon metanoein kai epistrephein epi ton Theon axia tēs metanoias erga prassontas
verses.literal: First to those in Damascus and Jerusalem then to everyone in the region of Judea and then to the Gentiles I declared that they should repent and turn to God performing deeds worthy of their repentance
verses.literalPt: mas anunciei primeiramente não só aos de Damasco e em Jerusalém e por toda a terra da Judeia, como também aos gentios, que se arrependessem e se convertessem a Deus, praticando obras dignas de seu arrependimento.

verses.original: ἕνεκα τούτων με Ἰουδαῖοι συλλαβόμενοι ὄντα ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἐπειρῶντο διαχειρίσασθαι
verses.transliteration: heneka toutōn me Ioudaioi syllabomenoi onta en tō hierō epeirōnto diacheirisasthai
verses.literal: For this reason . . . the Jews seized me in the temple courts and tried to kill me
verses.literalPt: Por isso, alguns judeus me prenderam no templo e procuravam matar-me.

verses.original: Ἐπικουρίας οὖν τυχὼν τῆς ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἄχρι τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης ἕστηκα μαρτυρόμενος μικρῷ τε καὶ μεγάλῳ οὐδὲν ἐκτὸς λέγων ὧν τε οἱ προφῆται ἐλάλησαν μελλόντων γίνεσθαι καὶ Μωϋσῆς
verses.transliteration: Epikourias oun tychōn tēs apo tou Theou achri tēs hēmeras tautēs hestēka martyromenos mikrō te kai megalō ouden ektos legōn hōn te hoi prophētai elalēsan mellontōn ginesthai kai Mōusēs
verses.literal: But I have had God’s help to this day and I stand here to testify to small and great alike I am saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen
verses.literalPt: Tendo, pois, obtido socorro da parte de Deus, permaneço até hoje, dando testemunho tanto a pequenos como a grandes, nada dizendo senão o que os profetas e Moisés disseram haver de acontecer,

verses.original: εἰ παθητὸς ὁ Χριστός εἰ πρῶτος ἐξ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν φῶς μέλλει καταγγέλλειν τῷ τε λαῷ καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν
verses.transliteration: ei pathētos ho Christos ei prōtos ex anastaseōs nekrōn phōs mellei katangellein tō te laō kai tois ethnesin
verses.literal: that the Christ would suffer and as the first to rise from the dead would proclaim light to our people and to the Gentiles
verses.literalPt: isto é, haver de sofrer o Cristo e que seria ele o primeiro que, pela ressurreição dos mortos, havia de anunciar a luz ao povo e aos gentios.

verses.original: Ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀπολογουμένου ὁ Φῆστος μεγάλῃ τῇ φωνῇ φησιν Μαίνῃ Παῦλε τὰ πολλά σε γράμματα εἰς μανίαν περιτρέπει
verses.transliteration: Tauta de autou apologoumenou ho Phēstos megalē tē phōnē phēsin Mainē Paule ta polla se grammata eis manian peritrepei
verses.literal: At this stage of Paul’s defense Festus exclaimed in a loud voice You are insane Paul Your great learning is driving you to madness
verses.literalPt: Aduzindo ele essas coisas em sua defesa, disse Festo em alta voz: Estás louco, Paulo! As muitas letras tiram-te o juízo.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Παῦλος Οὐ μαίνομαι φησίν Κράτιστε Φῆστε ἀλλὰ ἀληθείας καὶ σωφροσύνης ῥήματα ἀποφθέγγομαι
verses.transliteration: Ho de Paulos Ou mainomai phēsin Kratiste Phēste alla alētheias kai sōphrosynēs rhēmata apophthengomai
verses.literal: But Paul answered I am not insane most excellent Festus I am speaking words of truth and sobriety
verses.literalPt: Porém Paulo disse: Não estou louco, potentíssimo Festo, mas profiro palavras de verdade e de perfeito juízo.

verses.original: ἐπίσταται γὰρ περὶ τούτων ὁ βασιλεύς πρὸς ὃν καὶ παρρησιαζόμενος λαλῶ λανθάνειν γὰρ αὐτὸν τι τούτων οὐ πείθομαι οὐθέν οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἐν γωνίᾳ πεπραγμένον τοῦτο
verses.transliteration: epistatai gar peri toutōn ho basileus pros hon kai parrēsiazomenos lalō lanthanein gar auton ti toutōn ou peithomai outhen ou gar estin en gōnia pepragmenon touto
verses.literal: For the king knows about these matters and I can speak freely to him I am confident that none . . . of this has escaped his notice because it was not done in a corner
verses.literalPt: Pois dessas coisas tem conhecimento o rei, a quem falo também com franqueza, como persuadido estou de que nada disso lhe é oculto; porque isso não foi feito a um canto.

verses.original: πιστεύεις βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα τοῖς προφήταις οἶδα ὅτι πιστεύεις
verses.transliteration: pisteueis basileu Agrippa tois prophētais oida hoti pisteueis
verses.literal: King Agrippa do you believe the prophets I know you do
verses.literalPt: Crês, ó rei Agripa, os profetas? Eu sei que crês.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἀγρίππας πρὸς τὸν Παῦλον Ἐν ὀλίγῳ με πείθεις Χριστιανὸν ποιῆσαι
verses.transliteration: Ho de Agrippas pros ton Paulon En oligō me peitheis Christianon poiēsai
verses.literal: Then Agrippa said to Paul Can you persuade me in such a short time to become a Christian
verses.literalPt: Agripa disse a Paulo: Com pouco me persuades a fazer-me cristão.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Παῦλος Εὐξαίμην ἂν τῷ Θεῷ καὶ ἐν ὀλίγῳ καὶ ἐν μεγάλῳ οὐ μόνον σὲ ἀλλὰ καὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντάς μου σήμερον γενέσθαι τοιούτους ὁποῖος καὶ ἐγώ εἰμι παρεκτὸς τῶν δεσμῶν τούτων
verses.transliteration: Ho de Paulos Euxaimēn an tō Theō kai en oligō kai en megalō ou monon se alla kai pantas tous akouontas mou sēmeron genesthai toioutous hopoios kai egō eimi parektos tōn desmōn toutōn
verses.literal: Short time or long - Paul replied I wish to God that not only you but all who hear me this day may become what . . . I am except for these chains
verses.literalPt: Paulo respondeu: Prouvera a Deus que com pouco ou com muito não somente tu, mas ainda todos os que hoje me ouvem se tornassem tais qual eu sou, menos estas cadeias.

verses.original: Ἀνέστη τε ὁ βασιλεὺς καὶ ὁ ἡγεμὼν ἥ τε Βερνίκη καὶ οἱ συνκαθήμενοι αὐτοῖς
verses.transliteration: Anestē te ho basileus kai ho hēgemōn hē te Bernikē kai hoi synkathēmenoi autois
verses.literal: Then the king and the governor rose along with Bernice and those seated with them
verses.literalPt: O rei levantou-se, e também o governador, e Berenice, e os que estavam sentados com eles;

verses.original: καὶ ἀναχωρήσαντες ἐλάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους λέγοντες ὅτι Οὐδὲν θανάτου ἢ δεσμῶν ἄξιον τι πράσσει ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος
verses.transliteration: kai anachōrēsantes elaloun pros allēlous legontes hoti Ouden thanatou ē desmōn axion ti prassei ho anthrōpos houtos
verses.literal: On their way out they said to one another - This man has done nothing . . . worthy of death or imprisonment
verses.literalPt: e, havendo-se retirado, falavam uns com os outros, dizendo: Este homem nada tem feito que mereça morte ou prisão.

verses.original: Ἀγρίππας δὲ τῷ Φήστῳ ἔφη Ἀπολελύσθαι ἐδύνατο ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος εἰ μὴ ἐπεκέκλητο Καίσαρα
verses.transliteration: Agrippas de tō Phēstō ephē Apolelysthai edynato ho anthrōpos houtos ei mē epekeklēto Kaisara
verses.literal: And Agrippa said to Festus This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar
verses.literalPt: Agripa disse a Festo: Ele podia ser solto, se não tivesse apelado para César.
